question: Which distinctions in an entered GA chord symbol survive parsing, canonical rendering, and pitch-class projection, and how should a UI label those different representations?
production_path: investigation: observe hypothesize test conclude reflect
source reading: pin GA chord parser, AST, renderer, service, closure, and fixed tests
test: cross_validate five lesson answers against pinned source and checked-in assertions
hypothesis: Naming the entered sign, AST fields, canonical sign, and projected pitch class separately helps explain GA chord labels without treating code-level equivalence as a heard or context-independent musical judgment.
evidence: At GA commit dc2e74cbd992a298f67efb928b5b3754615e1924, Common/GA.Business.DSL/Parsers/ChordParser.fs defines root, accidental, optional quality, extension or alteration components, and optional slash bass; Common/GA.Business.DSL/Types/ChordAst.fs defines their AST fields.

At the same commit, Common/GA.Business.DSL/Services/ChordDslService.fs implements Normalize as Parse followed by Render, and Common/GA.Business.DSL/Generators/ChordRenderer.fs spells Minor as m and Major as maj.

The pinned Tests/Common/GA.Business.DSL.Tests/ChordDslTests.cs declares normalization cases Cmi7 to Cm7, D-7 to Dm7, EbΔ9 to Ebmaj9, and Fmaj7/A to Fmaj7/A. It also asserts root C and three components for C13#11b9. These tests were read, not rerun for this lesson.

The parser source treats maj7 as a whole Extension rather than a bare Major quality followed by 7; its source-derived Fmaj7/A AST has Quality=None, Extension maj7, and bass A. Its alternatives source-derive Extension 13 plus #11 and b9 Alterations for C13#11b9; the test only asserts the component count.

Common/GA.Business.DSL/Closures/BuiltinClosures/DomainClosures.fs calculates projectChord root and pc separately. Its source predicts C# and Db as distinct root spellings with the same root pitch class 1; the closure was not executed for this lesson.

The parser calls run pChord without an explicit end-of-input parser. This is a reason for a future boundary test, not an executed result about trailing input. Five source-based exercises have answers. Research duration was not instrumented; duration_seconds=0 records that limit.
